assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clean discovery from nature: a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos opened a new window on the universe. It was later backed by the TXS 0506+056 blazar association and by the Galactic-plane neutrino map. This is the kind of clue from nature I want, and it matters existentially for where cosmic accelerators are.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is widely seen as the intellectual driver of the IceCube concept and its science case, which makes a single-laureate award defensible. The detector was built by a large collaboration and AMANDA and other pioneers contributed, so a solo award leaves credit questions. The longlist supplies only Halzen as a credited name, so I cannot add others.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The discovery dates from about 2013, has been confirmed in several channels, and KM3NeT is adding independent cross-checks. The timing is good.
uncertainties: Whether a solo prize adequately reflects a collaboration-scale discovery and earlier detector pioneers.
Source identification beyond TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 is still limited, and I am recalling these results from memory rather than verifying them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of a non-zero theta13 settled a fundamental parameter of the lepton sector. It opened the path to CP violation searches in neutrinos. The result is a sharp, unambiguous discovery with a precise number behind it.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang, Luk), RENO and Double Chooz measured theta13 through reactor disappearance, and T2K (Nishikawa) saw electron-neutrino appearance. Daya Bay's precision was decisive, so Wang and Luk are the strongest pair. Whether T2K belongs alongside the reactor result is a judgment call. RENO and Double Chooz leaders are not in the supplied credited names.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The 2012 results were confirmed independently by multiple experiments and the value has been refined for over a decade.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to credit reactor and accelerator results together.
Competing priority claims among Daya Bay, RENO, Double Chooz and T2K, which I cannot settle from the supplied data.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory and experiment closely coupled: the Kane-Mele prediction, the HgTe quantum spin Hall observation, and the 3D topological insulator discovery with ARPES. It created a whole field of topological matter with broad conceptual reach.
assessment.attribution: Kane is the clear theoretical anchor. Molenkamp led the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state, and Hasan the first 3D topological insulator observation. Mele is a co-author of the key theory, and Bernevig, Zhang and others are outside the supplied names, so the configuration is contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature. About two decades of independent confirmation across materials. Practical applications remain modest, but the scientific impact is solid.
uncertainties: Credit divisions among Kane, Mele, Bernevig, Zhang, Molenkamp and Hasan, with some key theorists missing from the supplied list.
Whether a topological-matter prize should instead be built around the quantum anomalous Hall effect.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A predicted flat band at the magic angle was found, together with correlated insulators and superconductivity. It is a rare theory-led prediction confirmed in nature, and it started the moire materials field.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the theoretical prediction. Jarillo-Herrero's group found the experimental correlated and superconducting states in 2018. Andrei's early STM evidence is also important, but a three-person limit forces a choice.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature after about eight years of broad reproduction across many groups. The superconducting mechanism is still debated, though the discovery itself is secure.
uncertainties: Whether Andrei should displace Bistritzer, and how the committee weighs the mechanism question.
Some applications and derived effects are still moving.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A theory of neutron stars with magnetic fields around 10^15 G, tied to soft gamma repeaters and anomalous X-ray pulsars, then confirmed by observation. It links extreme physics to astronomical data, with a clear underlying idea.
assessment.attribution: Duncan and Thompson proposed the magnetar model in 1992, and Kouveliotou's measurement of the spin-down of SGR 1806-20 supported it. Paczynski's independent proposal is not in the supplied names. This is a natural theory-plus-observation configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the basic picture, with the 2020 Galactic fast radio burst from SGR 1935+2154 adding support. Details of the energy source and the FRB link remain active.
uncertainties: How central the magnetar picture is relative to the committee's other astrophysics priorities.
Open questions about the magnetar-FRB connection.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation, together with Mukhanov's calculation of quantum fluctuations seeding structure, accounts for the near scale-invariant spectrum measured in the CMB. The structure-origin part is a genuine, tested prediction.
assessment.attribution: Guth, Linde, Starobinsky, Albrecht and Steinhardt all contributed to the inflationary paradigm, and Mukhanov to the perturbation theory. Starobinsky is not in the supplied names. Whatever three-person configuration is chosen will leave out important contributors, which is a real problem.
assessment.maturity: Mixed. Perturbation predictions have been tested to high precision, but inflation itself still lacks a decisive signature such as primordial gravitational waves, and alternatives exist. I am wary of an elegant idea not yet fully confirmed, and I have written on trans-Planckian issues in inflation.
uncertainties: No detection of primordial B-modes, so the inflationary mechanism is not directly established.
The attribution is contested and the three-person limit cuts out key contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The acoustic scale imprinted in galaxy clustering provides a standard ruler that measures the expansion history, and so the nature of dark energy. It is directly relevant to the largest open question in cosmology, and DESI now adds interesting hints about dynamical dark energy.
assessment.attribution: The 2005 SDSS (Eisenstein) and 2dFGRS (Cole, Percival) detections were close in time. Peebles, Yu, Sunyaev and Zeldovich laid the theoretical basis. Hence the allocation is somewhat arbitrary and may favor the observers. The tool is a method more than a single discovery.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a technique, confirmed by many surveys. Its biggest implications, from DESI, are recent and not settled.
uncertainties: Whether this is a method rather than a discovery, which would weigh against it.
The DESI dark energy hints are evolving and could change the framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BeppoSAX X-ray afterglow detection and the optical redshift measurements showed that gamma-ray bursts are cosmological, resolving a decades-old puzzle. It is a discovery from nature that changed high-energy astrophysics.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX discovery of the afterglow, and the optical/redshift side involved van Paradijs, Djorgovski, Metzger and others. Kulkarni is a major figure, but the optical credit is spread. Credit is crowded and some key people are outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, as the result dates from 1997 and has been confirmed by Swift and many other missions. Recognition is arguably late.
uncertainties: Credit split between the X-ray and optical groups, with several deceased or omitted contributors.
Competition from more recent astrophysics discoveries for the same prize slot.
